newsitem.title: USA: SEC takes action vs. Arizona county in muni probe.
newsitem.headline: SEC takes action vs. Arizona county in muni probe.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said on Monday that it instituted cease and desist proceedings against Maricopa County, Ariz., seeking an order to stop the county from violating federal securities anti-fraud provisions.
The actions followed a probe of Maricopa County municipal bond deals by the SEC's Los Angeles office, the SEC said.
Maricopa County is the sixth largest county in the nation.

The SEC order instituting cease and desist proceedings alleged that the county violated the anti-fraud provisions of the federal securities laws in connection with the July 1993 offer and sale of two series of general obligation bonds.

The official statements for the offerings contained financial information about the county for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1992. The SEC said, however, that the county's financial condition at the time of the offerings had worsened since June 30, 1992. Specifically, the county had developed a deficit in its general fund, the SEC said.
During fiscal year 1992-1993, the county also had nearly doubled the deficit in its Medical Center Enterprise Fund.
"The official statements failed to disclose these changes," the SEC said in a statement.

The official statements also failed to disclose that the current liabilities of the Medical Center Enterprise Fund on June 30, 1993 exceeded its current assets by approximately 40 percent more than on June 30, 1992, the SEC said.
In addition, the SEC said the county's cash flow position had materially declined since the close of the prior fiscal year.
The SEC said official statements for one of the offerings represented that bond proceeds would be used to finance specific county projects.

"The county in fact planned to, and did, use the bond proceeds to finance its deficit through the end of the 1993-1994 fiscal year," the SEC said. But the county failed to revise or supplement its official statements, the SEC said.

"Each of the omitted items referenced above would have been important for an investor to consider in deciding whether or not to purchase the county's bonds because they tended to bear upon the county's financial condition at the time the bonds were issued," the SEC said.

Peacock, Hislop, Staley & Given Inc of Phoenix, Ariz., acted as the county's financial adviser for the deals. Gust Rosenfeld of Phoenix served as bond counsel. A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc was lead underwriter for one of the issues, while Goldman Sachs & Co was lead underwriter for the other.
The SEC declined to comment on whether its investigation of the deals would continue.
